_comment: The baseline WER ledger for egs/yesno/asr.
reference_wer is the number in egs/yesno/asr/README.md, measured by the
author on CUDA with torch 2.1. measured_wer is what this repository
produces now, on CPU with torch 2.15, recorded from the run named under
`measured`. max_wer is the gate.
The gate is measured_wer plus three word errors. test_yesno has 232
reference words, so one word error is 0.43%: the allowance absorbs a
different runner's floating-point rounding without admitting a real
regression, which on this corpus means tens of percent rather than
fractions of one.
Judge a change against measured_wer. **Raising max_wer to make a run
pass is how a ledger stops meaning anything** -- if a run exceeds the
gate, find out why.
utterances pins the data split. It is 31/29 rather than an even 30/30
because that is the split the published results were measured on: it
arose from two README files in the corpus being counted as waves, and
prepare_data.sh now states the count explicitly so that filtering them
out did not move an utterance across. 29 test utterances of eight words
each is the 232 above.
**Every number here was measured on 83-dimensional features** -- 80
filterbank coefficients plus the three pitch dimensions
process-kaldi-pitch-feats produces. Pitch was dropped in the PR that
added this note, so the model's input is 80 wide now and these are a
record of a configuration the recipe no longer has.
They are kept rather than cleared because they are the only
pre-refactor measurement that exists, and because the comparison that
matters is between the 83-dim and 80-dim eras: if yesno moves by more
than the gate allows, that is a real finding about pitch and not
noise. **max_wer has deliberately not been widened for the change.**
If an 80-dim run exceeds it, find out why -- which is what this file
is for.

measured.note: CPU, torch 2.15, with --dither=0 in conf/fbank.conf. reference_wer is the author's pre-refactor CUDA run at torch 2.1, kept as the historical record. Removing dither moved one word error in total across all eight topologies, downward.

features.note: pitch was a GMM-era addition for tonal languages; yesno is Hebrew and the gain is marginal. See CLAUDE.md.
